concepts.name: Fruitful
concepts.why: Name against passages: 'I will make you fruitful' is said (in the Berean's words) only in Gen 17:6 ('exceedingly fruitful'), 28:3, 48:4 and Lev 26:9. Gen 26:22 ('we will be fruitful', Isaac's own words), Gen 47:27 and Exod 1:7 are records that they became fruitful, and Jer 23:3 is 'they will be fruitful'. So the new name says more than half its passages, and the 'I will make you' voice is the very thing the records lack. A plain label 'Fruitful' is true of all eight and keeps the promises and their recording together. (Alternative: keep the name and drop Gen 26:22, 47:27 and Exod 1:7, but that loses the record that the promise took effect, which the texts themselves place side by side.) Notes are all exact quotations. No tradition takes a side here.

Asked directly: would any of the nine hear this grouping as taking a side on the Lord's Supper? No, as it now stands. (1) The group is built on a shared wording, not a doctrine: in the Berean every passage has 'spoke a blessing' (Matt 14:19; Luke 9:16; Matt 26:26; Mark 14:22; Luke 24:30) or 'the cup of blessing that we bless' (1 Cor 10:16), and in the Greek all six use the same verb family (eulogeo), so the original supports the grouping rather than the translation alone. (2) The name is two plain nouns and says nothing of Supper, Eucharist, communion, sacrament, memorial, presence or body and blood. (3) Every note quotes only the words of blessing. (4) The drafter has left out the cup of Matt 26:27 / Mark 14:23, where the texts say 'gave thanks' and not blessing, which keeps the group to what the words say; if that cup were added the group would begin to read as a Last Supper concept. Readers: Catholic, Orthodox and Lutheran would not object to the feedings and Emmaus standing beside the Supper (they would likely welcome it) but the group does not say it is a sacrament; Reformed, Wesleyan and Baptist/free-church readers who read the Supper as remembrance would not find the group claiming otherwise, since it asserts no 'is' of the bread or cup and the only 'participation' wording is 1 Cor 10:16's own; the secular/Jewish reader sees a repeated blessing formula over food and a cup, which is what the words are; the literary reader sees the repeated took-blessed-broke-gave pattern, which is observable without a theology. Watch-points, not changes: do not add a note or secondary line that calls any passage a Supper or links the feedings to it; and the bare name says 'cup' on the strength of 1 Cor 10:16 alone, which is true of the group as a whole, so it stands as a plain label. The passage texts of Matt 26:26 and Mark 14:22 carry 'this is My body' because the verse does; that is the text's own and no note leans on it.

secondary_or_links: Concept 3, Genesis 1:26 (optional, no change asked): the Berean's 'to rule over' reads the Hebrew as a purpose; the Hebrew is a plain 'let them rule', and whether the rule is the image's purpose is exactly where traditions and scholars divide. The note quotes only the words about ruling and the concept makes no claim about the image, so it stands; just keep any future note from tying rule to the image.

Link 'Church': harmless as a bare link, but it should not be read as saying that Abraham's blessing passes to the church (Israel and the church). It is kept only for the NT sendings and blessings (Matt 28:20; Acts; Rom 12:14; 1 Pet 3:9). If the link list is ever trimmed, it is the one a Baptist/dispensational or Jewish reader would most question.
Link 'Prophetic Word & Fulfillment' stays only for the prophets' commissions (Isa 6:8; Jer 1:7; Ezek 2:3), as the drafter says; no name or note says any passage is fulfilled.

New concept 5 (Blessed be Abram by God Most High): Hebrews 7 stands beside Genesis 14 as the passage in which the New Testament author takes up Melchizedek's blessing; the notes quote Hebrews' own words ('the lesser is blessed by the greater') and no name or note says Genesis 14 points to Hebrews, so it passes rule 4.
